subject: Oceanography
title: Mapping the Seafloor
description: A 60-second lesson on Mapping the Seafloor.

hook.text: We've mapped 100% of the Moon's surface but only about 25% of Earth's ocean floor in detail.

buildup.text: Early explorers used weighted ropes to measure depth—one sounding at a time, for miles of ocean.

discovery.text: Sonar changed everything in the 1920s—sound pulses bounce off the bottom and reveal its shape.

twist.text: Satellites can detect seafloor features from orbit by measuring tiny variations in sea surface height.

climax.text: Modern multibeam sonar maps wide swaths at once, but the deep ocean is vast and mostly unsurveyed.

punchline.text: The ocean floor is Earth's last unmapped frontier.
